key_insight: A reinforcement-learning agent merges micro-clusters into reactor zones optimized for lean blowout prediction, outperforming heuristic clustering for reduced-order combustor modeling.
engineering_relevance: This can speed up gas-turbine combustor design studies by giving more accurate LBO estimates than traditional reduced models while remaining much cheaper than high-fidelity chemistry simulations.
method: Start with an initial clustering step, such as k-means, to create many homogeneous micro-clusters.
Use an actor-critic RL agent to merge clusters into optimal liquid-fueled reactor zones.
Optimize cluster formation directly for the target metric, such as LBO prediction accuracy, rather than only input-space similarity.
evidence_signal: Validated on a Jet-A mechanism with 119 species and 841 reactions, the RL approach improved predictive fidelity, captured LBO trends correctly, and delivered substantial speedups over the high-fidelity model.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the initial micro-clustering and RL training setup, so gains may be sensitive to hyperparameters and the chosen combustion mechanism.
paper_title: A Reinforcement-Learning-Augmented Liquid-Fueled Reactor Network Model for Predicting Lean Blowout in Gas Turbine Combustors
